text:
Ria: Quick heads-up — onboarding sable-v2q (int8) into canary. We're seeing tool-call JSON parse failures jump ~+3.2% vs fp32 baseline, mostly in streaming responses and when tools are called with long KV prefixes. Not sure yet if it's tokenization or binary noise.

Sam: Can you paste a raw example?

Ria: Pasting sanitized excerpt — it's truncated but shows issue: 
```
...
{"tool": "search", "args": {"q": "find user\u0000name==\"alice\""}}
...
ERROR parse_json: unexpected token '\\u0000' at byte 123
```

Tess: Hmm looks like embedded nulls. Could be kv-cache prefix not being cleaned after quantized tokenizer emits control chars. I saw similar with micro-PTQ on zephyr.

Andre: Another possibility: int8 dequant rounding producing weird whitespace/control tokens mid-stream causing the stream parser to see non-utf8 bytes.

Ria: Telemetry snapshot: canary run 03/20 — parse_fail_rate int8: 2.8% -> 6.0% (fp32: 2.7%). Link: https://telemetry/redwood/sable-v2q-canary (short).

Sam: Two quick mitigation experiments: 1) disable KV-prefixing for canary requests, 2) add pre-parse sanitizer to drop non-printable bytes. Both low-risk.

Tess: Also add a parser fallback that attempts NDJSON-rescue: split on /}\n{/, wrap fragments and try reparsing. Less ideal but pragmatic for toolcalls.

Andre: Agreed. For longer-term, re-run tokenization diagnostics with int8 kernels and log raw token bytes around control chars. Might be a tokenizer table mismatch.

Ria: Ran sanitizer (stripping \u0000 and other C0 controls) in postprocess on a small sample (n=200). parse_fail reduced to +0.4% over fp32, but we now see ~0.7% semantic mis-mapping where tool name ended up in suffix text rather than as func call (ordering issues).

Sam: That suggests streaming boundary issues — retries or partial flushes are producing duplicated suffixes. When we retry we sometimes re-send prefix, toolcall appears mid-stream and our function-mapper picks it up as text.

Tess: Quick patch: 1) increase retry backoff and cap at 1 retry in canary, 2) make function-mapper tolerant to repeated tool tokens by preferring earliest well-formed object, 3) add sanitizer pre-join before streaming.

Andre: I'll add a lightweight token-byte-logger to the runtime for the canary bucket so we can correlate token bytes -> unicode sanitized output -> parser error. Low perf overhead if sampled.

canary-bot: Canary deploy initiated: sable-v2q-int8 (canary=kvprefix-off+sanitizer+retry-cap) — run id c-3312345678.

deploy-bot: Noted. Will surface canary metrics in 30m.

Ria: Action items: Tess to run canary with kvprefix off + sanitizer + retry-cap; Sam to add parser NDJSON-rescue fallback and prefer earliest valid funccall; Andre to enable sampled byte-logger; I'll collect 1k failing traces and attach.

Sam: I'll also add a temporary alert to catch parse-rate regressions >+1% vs baseline so we can roll back fast. :rotating_light:

Tess: Running now, ETA ~25m. Will post results in this thread.

Ria: Thanks — if this drops to acceptable delta we'll keep int8 canary but hold on broader rollout until tokenizer table check finishes.

Andre: If sanitizer + parser-rescue removes all parse failures but semantic mis-maps remain, we should consider a lightweight post-hoc structured-output reconciler that enforces schema and re-issues high-confidence function calls via deterministic mapping.

Ria: Agreed. Keep this thread for canary updates.
